claims.text: ADR 0028 puts reconciliation in Payments, owner of the refund rows and of the key refund-<id> it sends to the gateway; once a day a job fetches the previous day's report through the gateway's API and saves each line in Payments' database; the saved lines are owned by Payments.
Each report line is paired with a refund row by the key refund-<id>, because payments keeps no refund id of the gateway's; Payment.cs has no field for one.

In the lab, GET /v1/refunds on fake-gateway lists each refund with its idempotency key (and its own refund id rf-N, order, amount); the design assumes Gateway A's report carries the key, to be confirmed by the developer on the gateway integration.
Every comparison ends in one of five outcomes: matched; gateway refunded but row failed; gateway refund with no row; refunded row missing from the report; different amount.
A refunded row missing from the report becomes a difference only after one more run (assumed), because a refund near the end of a day may appear only in the next day's report.

The job changes no refund row; each difference goes to a list for staff; a correction is a new change made by a person and written to the audit log per docs/design/audit-log.md; staff propose, accounting approves (assumed roles).
A late report or a gateway failing during the run: the job runs again and a missed day is reported to accounting; report lines and results are kept as long as refund rows (both assumed).
Stage-4 has no reconciliation code; ADR 0028's header says only the ADR and the design review exist.

Deep dive: the gateway refunds, the answer is lost to a timeout; retries fail until YC-10's 24 hours end; the row becomes failed and payment.refund-failed is sent; the order moves from refunding back to paid and the customer is emailed that the refund failed.

claims.text: Normally Payments sends payment.refunded after the gateway refunds and the API calls Order.CompleteRefund(), moving a refunding order to cancelled; it accepts only a refunding order, so on a paid order its exception becomes a poison message and the message is dead-lettered.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs CompleteRefund; DonHang.Api/Messaging/PaymentEventsConsumer.cs lines 87-88, 107-113 @ stage-4; review lines 57-59 (quoted 42-59)

claims.text: The review records a new correction step moving a paid order to cancelled once reconciliation confirms the refund, an open question owned by the Ordering team, to design before reconciliation is built.
If Gateway A's report has no key, the review's risk table says to pair by order and amount, with more differences.
A refund row records no gateway; ADR 0028 is revisited when a second gateway is added per step 4 of ADR 0010's exit plan; the review assigns adding a gateway column to the backend developer.

Pairing on order and amount makes a refund whose amounts differ pair with nothing, so it shows as a refund with no row plus a missing row instead of one different amount; the key pairs regardless of amount.
claims.source_hint: derived from the five outcomes, ADR 0028 lines 40-42; review line 90 (more differences)

claims.text: Trade-offs: key vs order and amount; counting a missing row at once (a refund whose line arrives in the next day's report shows as a false difference) vs waiting one run; job overwrites vs list for staff with accounting approval.
Turning a failed row into refunded changes nothing in Ordering, so the order stays at paid; a late payment.refunded would not help, because CompleteRefund() accepts only a refunding order.
fake-gateway's comment says GatewayRefundClient translates the gateway's own language (refundId, reason, 422) and nothing else in Đơn Hàng sees it.
The saga's compensation adds a step and keeps the history rather than erasing what happened.
With the waiting rule, ĐS-3 (a refunded row missing from the report) is found within two days.

With a second gateway and no gateway column, searching both reports still pairs found lines, but a refunded row missing from both cannot say which report should have listed it (ADR 0028: each row must know its gateway, one report per gateway).
